chunks: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Mihran, from Ali ibn Uthman al-Razi, who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) say: 'Whoever is unable to visit us, let him visit the righteous of his brothers; it will be recorded for him as the reward of visiting us. And whoever is unable to reach us, let him reach the righteous of his brothers; it will be recorded for him as the reward of reaching us.'

key_terms.يُكْتَبْ لَهُ: it will be recorded for him

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting righteous believers if one cannot visit the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Hassan al-Awwan (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *ziyarat al-salihin* (visiting the righteous) as a valid substitute for direct pilgrimage to the Imams, emphasizing that spiritual proximity is maintained through the community of believers. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of the Imams as the spiritual axis (*al-qutb*) whose presence is accessible not only physically but also through the network of their devoted followers, ensuring that the reward of connection remains attainable for the broader Ummah.
